<reason>Both sides were disciplined and well structured, and PRO's opening plus its "fire exit" / "floor before the trend erodes" framing gave it real intuitive force. But CON did the sharper rebuttal work across the exchange: it dissolved PRO's alleged "contradiction" cleanly, caught PRO's inconsistency on whether unstaffed chain locations are covered (PRO first exempted them as "not major retailers," then, under Q1 pressure, said "covered"), and turned PRO's own compliance fallback ("stock that shelf with non-essentials") into the deleted-essentials-shelf that PRO had been denying. CON's central weighing — the mandate changes nothing for every named excluded shopper today and bites only at the thin-market margin — was never squarely refuted; PRO's precautionary answer was reasonable but CON pre-empted it as freezing today's retail format. PRO's best adaptation (bill-accepting machines) was a genuine counter, and CON's reply to the outage/resilience point ("puts no bill in wallet") was its weakest moment, which keeps this close. CON's honest refusal to invent a named town cost it rhetorically but was good epistemic discipline. Overall CON made the decision cleaner by exploiting PRO's own words; PRO won on rhetoric but lost ground on execution.</reason>
<best_rebuttal>CON's [B4.2]/[B5.3] turning PRO's "stock that shelf with non-essentials" into the deleted-essentials store "in PRO's own words," combined with the Q1 exposure of PRO's flip on whether unstaffed chain formats are covered.</best_rebuttal>
